To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the oxygen ion conductivity in mixed conducting perovskite-type oxides can be studied with the help of electron blocking microcontacts, (ii) the oxygen ion transport is a vacancy transport and (iii) the oxygen electrode reaction is a slow diffusion coupled red-ox process in the investigated manganites and in particular in Pr 0.3 Sr 0.7 MnO 3.

the oxygen electrode reaction in the mixed conducting perovskites Gd 0.8 Sr 0.2 CoO 1.9 and La 0.8 S r 0.2 FeO 1.95 is not limited by the surface reaction at the three phase boundary, air/YSZ/microcontact.

1) The oxygen ion conductivity in the perovskites Gd 0,8 Sr 0,2 CoO 2.9 and La 0,8Sr 0,2 FeO 2.95 was in the range of 1x10 -5 S/cm at 700°C and in the range of (1.2-2)x 10 -4 cm at 700°C, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of oxygen ion transport in mixed conductors.
the development of a new type of electrochemical gas sensor based on the use of mixed conductors.
the development of new mixed conducting materials for electrochemical sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Pr 0.7 Sr 0.3 MnO 2.9 is the best oxygen sensor electrode material in the investigated series of perovskites and that the manganites with a high Pr-content show a catalytic effect on the oxygen electrode reaction.
the oxygen electrode reaction is not catalyzed by the manganites investigated.
the oxygen electrode reaction is catalyzed at the surface of the mixed conductor in all cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the manganites investigated are not suitable materials for oxygen sensors, whereas Gd 0,8 Sr 0,2 CoO 1.9 and La 0,8Sr0.2FeO 1.95 show promising oxygen ion conductivities for application as oxygen sensors.
the oxygen electrode reaction is catalyzed by the manganites in air, but the oxygen ion transport in these oxides is too slow to allow for a fast response of the sensor.
the manganites are not mixed ionic and electronic conductors but rather oxygen ion conductors with a low oxygen ion conductivity and a catalytic activity of the surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxygen electrode reaction is catalyzed by the presence of a small amount of Mn 4+ cations.
the oxygen ion conductivity is not necessarily the most important factor for the catalytic activity of mixed conducting manganites.
it is possible to use microcontact measurements in combination with electron blocking microelectodes to study oxygen exchange and ion transport in mixed conductors.
